title: Analytic Weierstrass division after linear regularization
statement:
For an integer $d\geq0$, let $G_d$ be the commutative $\mathbf C$-algebra of germs at $0\in\mathbf C^d$ of holomorphic complex-valued functions: representatives are functions on open neighbourhoods of $0$, and two representatives agree when they agree on some smaller open neighbourhood. Holomorphic means locally representable by a convergent complex power series; operations and scalar multiplication are pointwise [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-function-operations]. For every $d\geq1$ and nonzero $f\in G_d$ there exist an invertible complex-linear map $L:\mathbf C^d\to\mathbf C^d$ and an integer $k\geq0$ such that, writing $h=f\circ L$, $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_{d-1})$ and $w=z_d$, one has $h(0,w)=w^k u(w)$ for a holomorphic one-variable germ $u$ with $u(0)\ne0$. For these choices, every $g\in G_d$ has a unique expression
$$g=q h+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}a_j(z)w^j,\qquad q\in G_d,\quad a_j\in G_{d-1}.$$
The germs $a_j$ are regarded in $G_d$ by composition with the coordinate projection $\mathbf C^d\to\mathbf C^{d-1}$. For $k=0$ the remainder sum is empty; for $d=1$ its coefficients belong to $G_0=\mathbf C$.

source.place: WANTED locally. J. Frenkel, Preliminaires a l etude de l anneau des fonctions analytiques a l origine, Seminaire H. Cartan 1951-52, exp.10, Proposition 4 (printed p.5, linear regularization), Theorem 1 (p.2, uniqueness) and Theorem 1 bis (pp.7-9, convergence of quotient and remainder), read online https://www.numdam.org/item/SHC_1951-1952__4__A10_0.pdf. Linear regularization for convergent series is also stated by F. Bruhat, same seminar exp.11, section 2, printed p.2, https://www.numdam.org/item/SHC_1951-1952__4__A11_0.pdf.

source.place: Proposition 4, printed p.5; section 4, pp.6-7; agent weighted-norm version; online source as in proof_origin.

proof.text: Fix any $L,k,u$ satisfying the asserted axis identity, so the remainder argument applies to every such choice. If $k=0$, $h(0)=u(0)\ne0$; [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-function-operations] gives $h^{-1}$, and the unique quotient is $q=gh^{-1}$ with empty remainder. Now assume $k\ge1$. Pull back the unit $u(w)$ along the last-coordinate projection and form $B=h/u(w)=w^k+c(z,w)$. The same analytic-operations node gives that $B,c$ and $1/u$ are holomorphic germs, and the axis identity gives $c(0,w)=0$. For a quotient $Q$ and remainder $R$ in a division by $B$, the equation $g=BQ+R$ is exactly $g=h(Q/u)+R$; thus it suffices to construct $Q$ uniquely.

source.place: Theorem 1, p.2 (unit normalization), and Theorem 1 bis, pp.7-9; agent weighted-norm version; online source as in proof_origin.

proof.text:
Fix $g$. By [lem-sfb-weighted-taylor-banach-model], choose common positive radii $(r^0,t)$ for the coefficient representatives of $g$ and $c$, decreasing finitely many initial radii componentwise. Write $n=d-1$ and use $r^0$ for the transverse radii and $t$ for the last radius. Since $c(0,w)=0$, restriction compatibility and injectivity in dimension one say that every coefficient $c_{0,j}$ is zero. For $n>0$ and $r=\lambda r^0$ with $0<\lambda\le1$, every remaining monomial has transverse degree at least one, so termwise comparison of absolute majorants gives
$$\|c\|_{r,t}\le\lambda\|c\|_{r^0,t}.$$
Choose $\lambda$ small enough that this is less than $t^k$ (if the original norm is zero any $\lambda$ works). The representative of $g$ stays in $A_{r,t}$ by the radius-decrease clause. When $n=0$, the axis is the entire space and $c=0$, so the same strict bound holds with no transverse radii. Set $A=A_{r,t}$.

source.place: Section 4, coefficient majorants, pp.6-7; section 5, shrinking transverse radii, p.8; agent weighted-norm version; online source as in proof_origin.

proof.text:
For a coefficient series $F=\sum_{\alpha,j}F_{\alpha,j}z^\alpha w^j$ in $A$, define
$$S_kF=\sum_{\alpha,j\ge k}F_{\alpha,j}z^\alpha w^{j-k},\qquad R_kF=\sum_{\alpha,j<k}F_{\alpha,j}z^\alpha w^j.$$
Their absolute majorants show $\|S_kF\|\le t^{-k}\|F\|$ and $\|R_kF\|\le\|F\|$, and coefficientwise $F=w^kS_kF+R_kF$. Multiplication by $c$ is bounded with norm at most $\|c\|$ by [lem-sfb-weighted-taylor-banach-model]. Hence $T(F)=S_k(cF)$ is bounded complex-linear and $\|T\|\le t^{-k}\|c\|<1$. Also $S_k(w^kF)=F$, and $S_kF=0$ holds exactly when all coefficients of $w$-degree at least $k$ vanish. These assertions follow directly by shifting or deleting the indicated summands; they invoke no division theorem.

source.place: Theorem 1 proof, pp.2-3 (coefficient-tail recurrence); section 5, pp.8-9 (majorants); agent weighted-norm version; online source as in proof_origin.

proof.text:
The space $A$ is complete by [lem-sfb-weighted-taylor-banach-model], so [lem-sfb-banach-small-operator-invertible] makes $I+T$ bijective. Set $Q=(I+T)^{-1}(S_kg)$ and $R=g-BQ$. Then
$$S_kR=S_kg-Q-S_k(cQ)=S_kg-(I+T)Q=0.$$
Thus $R=\sum_{j<k}a_j(z)w^j$. For each $j<k$, the coefficient slice has weighted transverse norm at most $t^{-j}\|R\|_{r,t}$, so it defines $a_j\in G_{d-1}$ by the weighted Taylor model. The same model sends $Q,R$ to holomorphic germs and respects multiplication. Taking $q=Q/u$ gives the required equation. If $d=1$, its dimension-zero clause identifies each $a_j$ with a complex number.

source.place: Theorem 1 bis, pp.7-9; agent Neumann-series implementation of its majorant recurrence; agent weighted-norm version; online source as in proof_origin.

proof.text: Suppose $g=hq'+R'$ is another asserted division, with $R'=\sum_{j<k}a'_j(z)w^j$, and put $Q'=uq'$. Choose smaller positive radii on which the coefficient representatives of $g,c,Q,Q',R,R'$ all belong to a common weighted algebra; this is possible for this finite list by [lem-sfb-weighted-taylor-banach-model]. Repeat the transverse shrinking of step 3 at its new last radius, so that again $\|S_k\circ M_c\|<1$. Injectivity of the germ map makes both division equations coefficient identities in that algebra. Subtract and apply $S_k$, which kills $R-R'$, obtaining $(I+T)(Q-Q')=0$. By [lem-sfb-banach-small-operator-invertible], $Q=Q'$, hence $q=q'$ since $u$ is a unit, and then $R=R'$. Equality of coefficients gives $a_j=a'_j$ as germs in dimension $d-1$. This rechoice of radii proves uniqueness among all germ quotients, without assuming a common original convergence disc for a competing solution.

source.place: Theorem 1, p.3 (uniqueness), with section 5, pp.7-9 (convergence); agent norm proof; agent weighted-norm version; online source as in proof_origin.
